recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. If Vocabulary wants more precise criteria for which displays or designations count as valid, that should be handled as a new decision that refines the current lenient-display-validation and displayLanguage semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-17218 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification STU3 Vocabulary request to clarify whether ValueSet $validate-code should return result=false when a supplied display is invalid, including whether validity depends on the value set display or another code designation. The accepted resolution was to say this was at implementer discretion while additional Vocabulary work on display validation expectations continued.
initial_application: No git commit in the current source history explicitly mentions FHIR-17218. The Jira comment says the change was already done, and the R4B/current OperationDefinition source imported in c69d71aa21 already contains the note that validation behavior for language on Coding.display is currently undefined and may receive later requirements or recommendations. Commit 60e98c41f6 later made only a spelling change to that note.
additional_context: ValueSet is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/valueset/operationdefinition-ValueSet-validate-code.xml is current build input. Later applied issue FHIR-41229 directly revisited the wrong-display true/false ambiguity and added lenient-display-validation: absent or false means an invalid display fails validation, while true makes display problems lenient. Earlier and later displayLanguage issues FHIR-10768 and FHIR-40770 provide the language-validation context. Confluence search found no FHIR-17218 reference, and the relevant Zulip thread supports the original uncertainty around foreign-language display validation.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reapplying broad implementer-discretion prose would conflict with the later, more specific R6 lenient-display-validation rule, while the remaining language/designation uncertainty is already represented by the current operation caveat.
